records.source: וַיְהִי֙ כַּאֲשֶׁר־תַּ֣מּוּ כָל־הַגּ֔וֹי לַעֲב֖וֹר אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ןפוַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And it was, when had finished all the nation crossing the Jordan, and said Yahweh to Joshua, saying,
pieces: When the entire nation had finished its crossing of the Jordan, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua,

L.1: And it came about, when all the nation had finished crossing the Jordan, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Joshua, saying,

R.1: All the people finished crossing the Jordan River. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua,

decisions.choice: all the nation: the whole people of Israel as one body
decisions.reason: The word usually names other peoples, but here, as in 3:17, it is used of Israel. The whole people, now on the west bank, is seen as one nation entering its land.

decisions.choice: when ... had finished crossing: the story picks up from the end of chapter 3
decisions.reason: Chapter 3 ended with the people crossing on dry ground while the priests stood with the ark in the riverbed (3:17). The priests are still standing there when the LORD gives the next command (verses 3, 10), so the stones are taken before the ark comes out.

decisions.choice: All the people
decisions.reason: Readable says "people" for "nation", the plainer word for young readers, and states the finished crossing as a sentence of its own.

records.heading: Twelve stones from the Jordan

records.source: קְח֤וּ לָכֶם֙ מִן־הָעָ֔ם שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר אֲנָשִׁ֑ים אִישׁ־אֶחָ֥ד אִישׁ־אֶחָ֖ד מִשָּֽׁבֶט׃
records.gloss: Take for yourselves from the people twelve men, a man one, a man one from [a] tribe.
pieces: "Choose twelve men from the people, one man from each tribe.

L.2: "Take for yourselves twelve men from the people, one man, one man from [each] tribe.

R.2: "Choose twelve men from the people, one man from each tribe.

decisions.choice: take for yourselves: a plural command, given to Joshua for the people's leaders to carry out with him
alternatives: the plural is addressed to all the people
decisions.reason: God speaks to Joshua (verse 1), but the verb is plural. Joshua is to see that it is done, with the leaders of the people; in verse 4 he calls the twelve men himself. The choosing of the twelve was already announced in 3:12.

decisions.choice: a man, one, a man, one, from a tribe: one man from each tribe
decisions.reason: Repeating a word in Hebrew can mean "each" or "every". The twelve men stand for the twelve tribes, so that every tribe has a part in the memorial (verse 5).

decisions.choice: Choose
decisions.reason: "Take" here means picking men out of the crowd for a task. Balanced and Readable say "choose".

records.source: וְצַוּ֣וּ אוֹתָם֮ לֵאמֹר֒ שְׂאֽוּ־לָכֶ֨ם מִזֶּ֜ה מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּ֗ן מִמַּצַּב֙ רַגְלֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים הָכִ֖ין שְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אֲבָנִ֑ים וְהַעֲבַרְתֶּ֤ם אוֹתָם֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם וְהִנַּחְתֶּ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם בַּמָּל֕וֹן אֲשֶׁר־תָּלִ֥ינוּ ב֖וֹ הַלָּֽיְלָה׃ס
records.gloss: And command them, saying, Take up for yourselves from here, from [the] middle of the Jordan, from [the] standing place of [the] feet of the priests, firmly, twelve stones; and carry them over with you, and set them down in the lodging place where you will spend the night in it the night.
pieces: Then command them, 'Pick up twelve stones from here in the middle of the Jordan, from the very spot where the priests have been standing firm. Carry them over with you, and set them down at the place where you camp tonight.'"

L.3: And command them, saying, 'Lift up for yourselves from here, from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the feet of the priests stood firm, twelve stones, and carry them over with you and set them down in the lodging place where you will lodge tonight.'"

R.3: Tell them, 'Pick up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, right where the priests are standing. Carry them across with you. Put them down at the place where you will stay tonight.'"

decisions.choice: firmly: the priests' feet stood fixed in one place
alternatives: take up twelve stones that have been made ready
the place where the priests' feet were set
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning "to make firm" or "to make ready". The same form in 3:17 says the priests stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, and that is the sense taken here. The accents of the Hebrew text join the word to what follows, which allows another reading: "prepare twelve stones", that is, have them made ready to carry.

decisions.choice: the lodging place: the place where the people would spend that night, at Gilgal
decisions.reason: The word names a place to stop for the night, such as a traveler's camp (Genesis 42:27). The people camp that night at Gilgal (verses 19-20), and the stones are set up there.

decisions.choice: for yourselves: a plural command to the twelve men
decisions.reason: From here on the command is spoken to the twelve men themselves, each of whom is to carry one stone (verse 5).

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the words the men are to hear
decisions.reason: The LORD's words to Joshua open with double quotation marks in verse 2. The command Joshua is to pass on is a quotation inside them, so it takes single marks, and both close at the end of this verse.

decisions.choice: right where the priests are standing
decisions.reason: Readable leaves the idea of standing "firm" in the plain word "standing", since the priests have not moved from the spot (verse 10).

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֣א יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ אֶל־שְׁנֵ֤ים הֶֽעָשָׂר֙ אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵכִ֖ין מִבְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִישׁ־אֶחָ֥ד אִישׁ־אֶחָ֖ד מִשָּֽׁבֶט׃
records.gloss: And called Joshua the twelve men whom he had appointed from [the] sons of Israel, a man one, a man one from [a] tribe.
pieces: So Joshua called together the twelve men he had chosen from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, one from each tribe.

L.4: And Joshua called the twelve men whom he had appointed from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, one man, one man from [each] tribe.

R.4: So Joshua called together the twelve men he had chosen from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, one man from each tribe.

decisions.choice: had appointed: had chosen and made ready beforehand
decisions.reason: The verb is from the same root as "firmly" in verse 3, "to make firm" or "to make ready". Joshua had already picked the men, as he was told to in 3:12.

decisions.choice: one man from each tribe
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ עִ֠בְרוּ לִפְנֵ֨י אֲר֧וֹן יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֖ם אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וְהָרִ֨ימוּ לָכֶ֜ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶ֤בֶן אַחַת֙ עַל־שִׁכְמ֔וֹ לְמִסְפַּ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֥י בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said to them Joshua, Cross over before [the] ark of Yahweh your God into [the] middle of the Jordan, and lift up for yourselves each [a] stone one on his shoulder, according to [the] number of [the] tribes of [the] sons of Israel,
pieces: Joshua said to them, "Go ahead of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, out to the middle of the Jordan. Every one of you is to lift a stone onto his shoulder, one for each of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}},

L.5: And Joshua said to them, "Cross over before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God into the middle of the Jordan, and lift up for yourselves, each man, one stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel,

R.5: Joshua told them, "Go out into the middle of the Jordan, in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Each of you must pick up a stone and carry it on your shoulder. There must be one stone for each tribe of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: cross over before the ark: go out into the riverbed, to where the ark stands
decisions.reason: The people have already crossed (verse 1), and the ark is still in the middle of the river with the priests (verse 10). The twelve men go back out from the bank, passing in front of the ark, to take stones from the spot where the priests are standing (verse 3).

decisions.choice: one stone on his shoulder: a large stone, each one a load for a man
decisions.reason: Each stone was big enough that a man had to carry it on his shoulder. Set up together, they would make a monument people could see (verse 20).

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 6
decisions.reason: Joshua's command and its purpose ("so that this may be a sign") are one sentence in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: There must be one stone for each tribe
decisions.reason: Readable ends the command here and starts the purpose as a new sentence in verse 6, so the sentences stay short.

records.source: לְמַ֗עַן תִּֽהְיֶ֛ה זֹ֥את א֖וֹת בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־יִשְׁאָל֨וּן בְּנֵיכֶ֤ם מָחָר֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֛ה הָאֲבָנִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: so that may be this [a] sign among you; when will ask your sons tomorrow, saying, What [are] the stones the these to you?
pieces: so that this will be a sign among you. In time to come, when your {{gender:children|sons}} ask, 'What do these stones mean to you?'

L.6: so that this may be a sign among you. When your {{gender:children|sons}} ask tomorrow, saying, 'What [are] these stones to you?'

R.6: These stones will be a sign for you. Someday your {{gender:children|sons}} will ask you, 'What do these stones mean?'

decisions.choice: a sign: something to see that points to what God has done
decisions.reason: A "sign" here is a reminder that can be seen and that calls for an explanation, like the Passover meal and the feast of unleavened bread (Exodus 13:9) or the twelve stones of the altar at Sinai (Exodus 24:4).

decisions.choice: tomorrow: in time to come
decisions.reason: "Tomorrow" here means any day in the future, as in Exodus 13:14 and Deuteronomy 6:20.

decisions.choice: the question of the children: the way the law teaches the next generation
decisions.reason: The pattern of a child asking and a parent explaining is the pattern of the Passover (Exodus 12:26-27; 13:14) and of the law as a whole (Deuteronomy 6:20-25). The stones will open the same kind of conversation.

decisions.choice: What do these stones mean (to you)?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "What are these stones to you?" asks what they stand for. Balanced and Readable put it as English asks it.

decisions.choice: children, with "sons" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of "son", but here it means the next generation, girls as well as boys.

records.source: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֣ם לָהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִכְרְת֜וּ מֵימֵ֤י הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ מִפְּנֵי֙ אֲר֣וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֔ה בְּעָבְרוֹ֙ בַּיַּרְדֵּ֔ן נִכְרְת֖וּ מֵ֣י הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וְ֠הָיוּ הָאֲבָנִ֨ים הָאֵ֧לֶּה לְזִכָּר֛וֹן לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: then you will say to them that were cut off [the] waters of the Jordan before [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh; when it crossed over into the Jordan, were cut off [the] waters of the Jordan; and will be the stones the these for [a] memorial for [the] sons of Israel until forever.
pieces: then tell them, 'In front of the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the waters of the Jordan were cut off. As it passed into the Jordan, the Jordan's waters were cut off.' These stones will be a memorial for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} forever."

L.7: then you shall say to them that the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; when it crossed over into the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. And these stones shall be for a memorial to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel forever."

R.7: Then you will tell them, 'The water of the Jordan stopped flowing in front of the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. When the ark went across the river, the water stopped.' These stones will always help the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} remember what happened."

decisions.choice: were cut off: stopped flowing and were held back
decisions.reason: The verb means "to cut" or "to cut off". Said of a river, it means the flow was stopped, as 3:13 and 3:16 describe: the water coming down stood up in a heap far upstream, and the water below ran off to the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: the words "were cut off" are said twice for emphasis
decisions.reason: The answer repeats the main fact, first with the ark ("before the ark") and then with the moment ("when it crossed"). The repetition stresses that the ark of the covenant, the sign of God's presence, is what stopped the river.

decisions.choice: memorial: a reminder that keeps an event in the people's memory
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to remember". A memorial calls something to mind for the people and before God (Exodus 12:14; 28:12; Numbers 17:5 in the Hebrew numbering).

decisions.choice: the answer to the children ends with "cut off"; the last sentence is Joshua's word to the men
alternatives: the parents' answer runs to the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no quotation marks. The answer the parents are to give is the account of the waters; the closing words about a memorial "forever" read as Joshua's own statement of what the stones are for. They could also be taken as part of the answer.

decisions.choice: direct quotation for "that ..."
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "say to them that ...". Balanced and Readable give the parents' answer as their own words, in single quotation marks inside Joshua's speech.

decisions.choice: will always help ... remember what happened
decisions.reason: Readable explains "memorial" by what it does, and says "always" for "until forever".

records.source: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֣ן בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֘לכַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֒ וַיִּשְׂא֡וּ שְׁתֵּֽי־עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה אֲבָנִ֜ים מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּ֗ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ לְמִסְפַּ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּעֲבִר֤וּם עִמָּם֙ אֶל־הַמָּל֔וֹן וַיַּנִּח֖וּם שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And did so [the] sons of Israel just as commanded Joshua, and they lifted up twelve stones from [the] middle of the Jordan, just as spoke Yahweh to Joshua, according to [the] number of [the] tribes of [the] sons of Israel; and they carried them over with them to the lodging place and set them down there.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did as Joshua commanded. They lifted twelve stones out of the middle of the Jordan, one for each of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Joshua. They took them across to the camping place and laid them down there.

L.8: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did so, just as Joshua commanded, and they lifted up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; and they carried them over with them to the lodging place and set them down there.

R.8: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what Joshua told them. Just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Joshua, they took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, one stone for every tribe of Israel. They carried the stones to the place where they camped for the night and put them down there.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel did so: the whole people acted through the twelve men
decisions.reason: The twelve men did the carrying (verse 5), but the verse says "the sons of Israel" did it. Each man stood for his tribe, so what they did, all Israel did.

decisions.choice: just as Joshua commanded ... just as the LORD had spoken: Joshua's order carries the LORD's word
decisions.reason: The verse names both: the people obey Joshua, and in doing so they do what the LORD told Joshua (verses 1-3). Verse 10 adds Moses to the chain, and the chapter shows Joshua as a leader whose word can be trusted because it comes from God (verse 14).

decisions.choice: one for each of the tribes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable move "according to the number of the tribes" next to "twelve stones", where it belongs in English, and say it as "one for each".

records.source: וּשְׁתֵּ֧ים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אֲבָנִ֗ים הֵקִ֣ים יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֮ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּן֒ תַּ֗חַת מַצַּב֙ רַגְלֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים נֹשְׂאֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן הַבְּרִ֑ית וַיִּ֣הְיוּ שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And twelve stones set up Joshua in [the] middle of the Jordan, in place of [the] standing place of [the] feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant; and they have been there until the day the this.
pieces: In the middle of the Jordan, Joshua also set up twelve stones, at the spot where the priests carrying the ark of the covenant had stood. They are there to this day.

L.9: And twelve stones Joshua set up in the middle of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant had stood; and they have been there to this day.

R.9: Joshua also set up twelve stones out in the middle of the Jordan River, at the place where the priests carrying the ark of the covenant had stood. Those stones are still there today.

decisions.choice: a second set of twelve stones, set up in the riverbed itself
alternatives: the same twelve stones as in verses 8 and 20, taken from the middle of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The verse says the stones were set up "in the middle of the Jordan", where the priests had stood, while the stones the men carried were set up at Gilgal (verses 8, 20). Putting "twelve stones" first in the sentence suggests a new subject, and the ancient Greek translation reads "other twelve stones". Some take the verse to describe the same stones as verse 8, reading "in the middle of the Jordan" as where they were taken from, but the wording speaks of setting them up in that place.

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the time the book was written
decisions.reason: The phrase is the writer's note that the stones could still be seen in his own time. It comes often in Joshua (5:9; 7:26; 8:28-29).

decisions.choice: also
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "also" to show that this is a second set of stones, as decision m1 explains. Literal keeps the bare Hebrew.

records.source: וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֞ים נֹשְׂאֵ֣י הָאָר֗וֹן עֹמְדִים֮ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּן֒ עַ֣ד תֹּ֣ם כָּֽל־הַ֠דָּבָר אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־הָעָ֔ם כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ וַיְמַהֲר֥וּ הָעָ֖ם וַֽיַּעֲבֹֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: And the priests carrying the ark [were] standing in [the] middle of the Jordan until was finished every the thing which commanded Yahweh Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that commanded Moses Joshua; and hurried the people and crossed over.
pieces: The priests who carried the ark kept standing in the middle of the Jordan until everything was done that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Joshua to tell the people, just as Moses had commanded Joshua. And the people crossed over in haste.

L.10: And the priests carrying the ark [were] standing in the middle of the Jordan until every thing was finished that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua; and the people hurried and crossed over.

R.10: The priests carrying the ark stayed in the middle of the Jordan until the people had done everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told Joshua to tell them. It was all just as Moses had told Joshua. The people hurried across the river.

decisions.choice: every thing: every matter, all that had to be done
decisions.reason: The word can mean "word" or "thing". Here it is everything the LORD had told Joshua to have the people do at the crossing, including the taking of the stones.

decisions.choice: according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua: Moses' charge to Joshua to lead Israel across
decisions.reason: No command of Moses about the details of the crossing is recorded. The phrase points back to the charge Moses gave Joshua to take the people over the Jordan and into the land (Deuteronomy 3:28; 31:7-8, 23), which Joshua is now carrying out.

decisions.choice: the people hurried and crossed over: a look back at the crossing itself
decisions.reason: The verse returns to the people's crossing (3:17; 4:1). It does not say why they hurried; the priests were standing in the riverbed the whole time, holding back the water by the ark.

decisions.choice: It was all just as Moses had told Joshua.
decisions.reason: Readable makes the reference to Moses a short sentence of its own.

records.source: וַיְהִ֛י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־תַּ֥ם כָּל־הָעָ֖ם לַֽעֲב֑וֹר וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר אֲרוֹן־יְהוָ֛ה וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was, when had finished all the people crossing over, and crossed over [the] ark of Yahweh and the priests before the people.
pieces: When all the people had finished crossing, the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the priests crossed over in front of the people.

L.11: And it came about, when all the people had finished crossing over, that the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} crossed over, and the priests, before the people.

R.11: When all the people were across, the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the priests crossed over too, in front of the people.

decisions.choice: the ark crossed over: a short summary, told in detail in verses 15-18
decisions.reason: The verse tells the end of the crossing in a few words. Verses 15-18 go back and tell how the LORD ordered the priests out of the river and how the water came back.

decisions.choice: before the people: in front of them, in their sight
alternatives: in full view of the people
ahead of the people, at their head
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "in the sight of" the people, who watched the ark come out, or "ahead of" them, as the ark again took its place at the head of the people (3:6). Both fit; the wording is kept open.

records.source: וַ֠יַּעַבְרוּ בְּנֵי־רְאוּבֵ֨ן וּבְנֵי־גָ֜ד וַחֲצִ֨י שֵׁ֤בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁה֙ חֲמֻשִׁ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And crossed over [the] sons of Reuben and [the] sons of Gad and half of [the] tribe of the Manasseh, armed, before [the] sons of Israel, just as had spoken to them Moses.
pieces: The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh went across armed for battle, ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, as Moses had told them.

L.12: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, just as Moses had spoken to them.

R.12: The fighting men from the tribes of Reuben and Gad and from half of the tribe of Manasseh went across ahead of the other {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They were ready for battle, just as Moses had told them to be.

decisions.choice: just as Moses had spoken to them: the promise of the tribes that settled east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh received land east of the Jordan on one condition: their fighting men would cross ahead of the other tribes and fight until the whole land was taken (Numbers 32:20-32; Deuteronomy 3:18-20). Joshua reminded them of it before the crossing (1:12-18), and here they keep their word.

decisions.choice: armed: ready for war, perhaps drawn up in battle order
decisions.reason: The word is used of Israel leaving Egypt "armed" or "in battle array" (Exodus 13:18) and of these same tribes in 1:14. Its exact sense is not certain: it may mean equipped for battle, or marching in ranks. Either way they crossed as soldiers.

decisions.choice: the sons of Reuben and of Gad: their fighting men
decisions.reason: The verse means the warriors of these tribes, not the whole tribes. Their families and herds stayed on the east side (1:14; Numbers 32:26-27), and verse 13 gives their number.

decisions.choice: the Reubenites, the Gadites (Balanced); the fighting men from the tribes (Readable)
decisions.reason: These are men of war, so no gender setting applies. Balanced uses the tribe names, as Numbers 32 does; Readable says plainly that the fighting men are meant.

records.source: כְּאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף חֲלוּצֵ֣י הַצָּבָ֑א עָבְר֞וּ לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה אֶ֖ל עַֽרְב֥וֹת יְרִיחֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: About forty thousand equipped [for] the army crossed over before Yahweh for the battle, to [the] plains of Jericho.
pieces: About 40,000 men equipped for war crossed over before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, ready for battle, to the plains of Jericho.

L.13: About 40,000 equipped for the army crossed over before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for battle, to the plains of Jericho.

R.13: About 40,000 soldiers went across in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the plains near Jericho. They were armed and ready to fight.

decisions.choice: about forty thousand: the part of the eastern tribes' fighting men who crossed
decisions.reason: The census on the plains of Moab counted over 110,000 men of fighting age in Reuben, Gad and the whole of Manasseh (Numbers 26:7, 18, 34). Forty thousand were sent over; others stayed behind with the families and herds (Numbers 32:16-17). On the size of the word "thousand", see the note at Numbers 1:21.

decisions.choice: equipped for the army: men armed and ready for war
decisions.reason: The word describes men stripped for action and armed (Numbers 32:21, 27, 29). Joined to the word for an army, it means men fit and equipped for military service.

decisions.choice: before the LORD: in the presence of the LORD, whose ark went with them
decisions.reason: The ark was the sign of the LORD's presence among his people (3:10-11). To march "before the LORD" is to go out under his eye and at his command; the battle is his (5:13-15; 6:2).

decisions.choice: the plains of Jericho: the flat floor of the Jordan valley around the city
decisions.reason: The valley west of the river is a wide, low plain. Jericho, an oasis city, stood at its western edge, about five miles from the river.

decisions.choice: men (Balanced); soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "equipped ones" has no noun. Balanced and Readable supply one, since these are the fighting men of verse 12.

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא גִּדַּ֤ל יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ בְּעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּֽרְא֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יָרְא֥וּ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֖ה כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: On the day the that made great Yahweh Joshua in [the] eyes of all Israel; and they feared him just as they had feared Moses, all [the] days of his life.
pieces: That day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raised Joshua up in the sight of all Israel, and they held him in awe all his life, just as they had held Moses in awe.

L.14: On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they feared him, just as they had feared Moses, all the days of his life.

R.14: That day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made all Israel see how great a leader Joshua was. They respected him deeply for as long as he lived, just as they had respected Moses.

decisions.choice: the LORD made Joshua great: the promise of 3:7 kept
decisions.reason: Before the crossing the LORD said, "Today I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel, so that they may know that as I was with Moses, I will be with you" (3:7). The parting of the Jordan, like the parting of the sea under Moses (Exodus 14:31), shows the people that God stands behind their leader.

decisions.choice: feared: held in awe and respected as God's chosen leader
decisions.reason: The verb means "to fear", but said of people toward a leader God has set over them it means deep respect and readiness to obey, not terror. After the sea, Israel "feared the LORD and believed in the LORD and in his servant Moses" (Exodus 14:31).

decisions.choice: all the days of his life: Joshua's life
alternatives: just as they had feared Moses all the days of Moses' life
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew the phrase comes after "Moses", so it could mean that Israel feared Moses all his life. But the point of the verse is how Joshua was regarded from that day on, and the phrase is taken with "they feared him".

decisions.choice: made all Israel see how great a leader Joshua was; respected him deeply
decisions.reason: Readable explains "made great in the eyes of" and puts "feared" as deep respect, which is the sense here (decision m2).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Joshua, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua,

L.15: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Joshua, saying,

decisions.choice: the story goes back to the moment before the ark came up
decisions.reason: Verse 11 has already said that the ark crossed. Verses 15-18 now tell how it happened: the LORD gave the order, Joshua passed it on, and the water returned as the priests stepped out.

records.heading: The stones set up at Gilgal

records.source: צַוֵּה֙ אֶת־הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים נֹשְׂאֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן הָעֵד֑וּת וְיַעֲל֖וּ מִן־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: Command the priests carrying [the] ark of the testimony, and let them come up from the Jordan.
pieces: "Order the priests carrying the ark of the testimony to come up from the Jordan."

L.16: "Command the priests carrying the ark of the testimony that they come up from the Jordan."

R.16: "Tell the priests carrying the ark that holds the covenant tablets to come up out of the Jordan."

decisions.choice: the ark of the testimony: the ark that held the tablets of the covenant
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the name for the two stone tablets of the covenant, which were kept in the ark (Exodus 25:16, 21-22; 31:18). This is the only place in Joshua that uses this name for the ark; elsewhere in these chapters it is "the ark of the covenant".

decisions.choice: the ark that holds the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable explains "testimony", as it does in Exodus, so young readers know what is meant.

records.source: וַיְצַ֣ו יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ אֶת־הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר עֲל֖וּ מִן־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And commanded Joshua the priests, saying, Come up from the Jordan.
pieces: So Joshua commanded the priests, "Come up out of the Jordan."

L.17: And Joshua commanded the priests, saying, "Come up from the Jordan."

R.17: So Joshua gave the order to the priests: "Come up out of the Jordan."

decisions.choice: Joshua passes on the LORD's word as it was given
decisions.reason: The priests move only when the LORD gives the word through Joshua. The order in verse 16 and Joshua's command here use the same verb, "come up", so his word is shown to be the LORD's word.

records.source: וַ֠יְהִי כַּעֲל֨וֹת הַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים נֹשְׂאֵ֨י אֲר֤וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָה֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן נִתְּק֗וּ כַּפּוֹת֙ רַגְלֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים אֶ֖ל הֶחָרָבָ֑ה וַיָּשֻׁ֤בוּ מֵֽי־הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ לִמְקוֹמָ֔ם וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ כִתְמוֹל־שִׁלְשׁ֖וֹם עַל־כָּל־גְּדוֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And it was, as came up the priests carrying [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh from [the] middle of the Jordan, were drawn out [the] soles of [the] feet of the priests to the dry ground, and returned [the] waters of the Jordan to their place and went as yesterday [and] three days ago over all its banks.
pieces: As the priests who carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stepped up from the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of their feet came out onto dry ground, the Jordan's waters went back to their place and flowed over all its banks as they had before.

L.18: And it came about, as the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came up from the middle of the Jordan, [and] the soles of the feet of the priests were pulled up onto the dry ground, that the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and went as before over all its banks.

R.18: The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} climbed up out of the middle of the river. As soon as their feet stepped up onto dry ground, the water of the Jordan came back. It flowed over all its banks again, just as it had before.

decisions.choice: the soles of the feet were pulled up onto the dry ground: the priests stepped out of the riverbed onto the bank
decisions.reason: The verb means "to be pulled away" or "torn loose", as a foot is pulled free from the ground. The priests had stood in the riverbed from the start (3:15-17); the moment their feet came up out of it onto the dry ground, the river returned. The same feet that stopped the water when they touched it (3:13, 15) let it go when they left.

decisions.choice: as yesterday and the day before: as it had before
decisions.reason: "Yesterday and the day before" means "formerly", "as usual" (Genesis 31:2; Exodus 5:7).

decisions.choice: over all its banks: in spring flood
decisions.reason: The crossing took place at harvest time, when the Jordan overflows its banks (3:15) from the rains and the melting snow of Mount Hermon. The return of the flood shows that the dry crossing had been God's doing, not a low river.

decisions.choice: [and]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the two clauses about the priests side by side. Literal supplies "and" in brackets so the long sentence can be followed.

decisions.choice: as before / as they had before / just as it had before
decisions.reason: The idiom is given by its meaning at every level, since "as yesterday and three days ago" would mislead in English. The literal gloss keeps the Hebrew words.

records.source: וְהָעָ֗ם עָלוּ֙ מִן־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן בֶּעָשׂ֖וֹר לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בַּגִּלְגָּ֔ל בִּקְצֵ֖ה מִזְרַ֥ח יְרִיחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And the people came up from the Jordan on [the] tenth of the month the first, and they camped at the Gilgal on [the] edge of [the] east of Jericho.
pieces: On the tenth day of the first month the people came up out of the Jordan and camped at Gilgal, on Jericho's eastern border.

L.19: And the people came up from the Jordan on the tenth of the first month, and they camped at Gilgal, on the eastern edge of Jericho.

R.19: On the tenth day of the first month, the people came up out of the Jordan. They set up camp at Gilgal, at the eastern edge of the land around Jericho.

decisions.choice: the tenth of the first month: the day the Passover lamb was chosen, forty years after the exodus
decisions.reason: The first month, in spring, was the month of the Passover (Exodus 12:2; 13:4). On its tenth day each household chose its lamb (Exodus 12:3), and four days later Israel kept the Passover at Gilgal (5:10). The people left Egypt in this month (Numbers 33:3) and now enter the land in it, forty years on (5:6).

decisions.choice: Gilgal: Israel's first camp in the land, between the Jordan and Jericho
decisions.reason: The site is not known for certain. It became the base camp for the early campaigns (9:6; 10:6) and a holy place in later times (1 Samuel 11:14-15). The name sounds like the verb "to roll", which 5:9 explains.

decisions.choice: the eastern edge of Jericho: the east side of the city's territory
decisions.reason: "Jericho" here means the city with its lands. Gilgal lay at their eastern edge, toward the river.

decisions.choice: the tenth day
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "the tenth of the month"; Balanced and Readable add "day", as English dates require.

records.source: וְאֵת֩ שְׁתֵּ֨ים עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה הָֽאֲבָנִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֖וּ מִן־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן הֵקִ֥ים יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בַּגִּלְגָּֽל׃
records.gloss: And twelve the stones the these which they had taken from the Jordan, set up Joshua at the Gilgal.
pieces: Joshua set up at Gilgal the twelve stones they had taken from the Jordan.

L.20: And those twelve stones that they had taken from the Jordan, Joshua set up at Gilgal.

R.20: At Gilgal, Joshua set up the twelve stones the men had taken out of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: those twelve stones: the stones the twelve men carried (verse 8)
decisions.reason: The stones come first in the Hebrew sentence to tie them back to verses 3-8. These are the stones taken from the riverbed and carried to the camp, not the ones set up in the river (verse 9).

decisions.choice: set up: stood them upright as a monument
decisions.reason: The verb means "to raise" or "to make stand". The stones were set up where all could see them, as Jacob and Moses set up stones as witnesses (Genesis 31:45-46; Exodus 24:4).

decisions.choice: the men
decisions.reason: Readable names who took the stones (verse 8), since "they" would be unclear at the start of a new section.

records.source: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר אֲשֶׁר֩ יִשְׁאָל֨וּן בְּנֵיכֶ֤ם מָחָר֙ אֶת־אֲבוֹתָ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֖ה הָאֲבָנִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And he said to [the] sons of Israel, saying, When will ask your sons tomorrow their fathers, saying, What [are] the stones the these?
pieces: Then he said to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "In time to come, when your {{gender:children|sons}} ask their {{gender:parents|fathers}}, 'What do these stones mean?'

L.21: And he said to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, "When your {{gender:children|sons}} ask their {{gender:parents|fathers}} tomorrow, saying, 'What [are] these stones?'

R.21: Joshua told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "Someday your {{gender:children|sons}} will ask their {{gender:parents|fathers}}, 'What do these stones mean?'

decisions.choice: tomorrow: in time to come
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

decisions.choice: your children ... their fathers: the fathers are the people Joshua is speaking to
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves from "your" to "their" in one clause. Those who crossed are the fathers of the children who will ask; Joshua speaks to them about their own children.

decisions.choice: the children's question: the same as in verse 6
decisions.reason: Verses 21-24 repeat for the whole people what Joshua told the twelve men in verses 6-7, and add what the crossing was for (verse 24).

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he said". Readable names Joshua, who set up the stones in verse 20.

decisions.choice: children / parents, with "sons" / "fathers" as the alternatives
decisions.reason: The question and answer are for the whole next generation and their parents, mothers as well as fathers.

records.source: וְהוֹדַעְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־בְּנֵיכֶ֣ם לֵאמֹ֑ר בַּיַּבָּשָׁה֙ עָבַ֣ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: then you will make known [to] your sons, saying, On dry ground crossed Israel the Jordan the this.
pieces: then explain it to your {{gender:children|sons}}: 'Israel crossed this Jordan on dry ground.'

L.22: then you shall make known to your {{gender:children|sons}}, saying, 'On dry ground Israel crossed this Jordan.'

R.22: Then you will tell your {{gender:children|sons}}, 'Israel walked across this Jordan River on dry ground.'

decisions.choice: on dry ground: the same words as for the crossing of the sea
decisions.reason: "Dry ground" is the word used when Israel crossed the sea out of Egypt (Exodus 14:16, 22, 29). The answer puts the two crossings side by side, as verse 23 says outright.

decisions.choice: Israel crossed: the people as one, with a singular verb
decisions.reason: The answer speaks of "Israel" as one person. The children who ask are part of that Israel, so the crossing becomes their story too.

decisions.choice: walked across
decisions.reason: Readable says "walked across" to make the picture of crossing a riverbed on foot plain.

records.source: אֲשֶׁר־הוֹבִישׁ֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֜ם אֶת־מֵ֧י הַיַּרְדֵּ֛ן מִפְּנֵיכֶ֖ם עַֽד־עָבְרְכֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֧ם לְיַם־ס֛וּף אֲשֶׁר־הוֹבִ֥ישׁ מִפָּנֵ֖ינוּ עַד־עָבְרֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: for dried up Yahweh your God [the] waters of the Jordan from before you until you had crossed over, just as did Yahweh your God to [the] Sea of Reeds, which he dried up from before us until we had crossed over,
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God dried up the Jordan's waters ahead of you until you had crossed, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God had done to the Red Sea, drying it up ahead of us until we had crossed,

L.23: for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed over, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did to the Sea of Reeds, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dried up before us until we had crossed over,

R.23: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God dried up the water of the Jordan in front of you until you were all across. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God did the same thing at the Red Sea. He dried it up in front of us until we had crossed.

decisions.choice: the answer to the children ends with verse 22; verses 23-24 are Joshua's words to Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no quotation marks. Verse 23 begins "for" and speaks of what God did "before you ... until you crossed", which fits Joshua speaking to those who had just crossed. The words could also be heard as part of what the parents are to tell their children.

decisions.choice: just as ... to the Sea of Reeds: the crossing of the sea out of Egypt
decisions.reason: The LORD drove back the sea and made it dry land, and Israel went through on dry ground (Exodus 14:21-22). The Jordan crossing repeats that wonder for the generation entering the land.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the sea Israel crossed out of Egypt
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name means "sea of reeds". It is the sea of the exodus (Exodus 15:4) and is also used of the Gulf of Aqaba (1 Kings 9:26). Its exact location for the crossing is not certain.

decisions.choice: before us ... we: Joshua counts himself among those who crossed the sea
decisions.reason: Joshua had come out of Egypt as a young man (Exodus 17:9; 33:11; Numbers 14:30). He says "we" of the sea and "you" of the Jordan, and so joins the two generations in one story.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea (Balanced, Readable); the Sea of Reeds (Literal)
decisions.reason: Literal gives the Hebrew name. Balanced and Readable use the name known to most readers, as Exodus 15:4 does.

records.source: לְ֠מַעַן דַּ֜עַת כָּל־עַמֵּ֤י הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֶת־יַ֣ד יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י חֲזָקָ֖ה הִ֑יא לְמַ֧עַן יְרָאתֶ֛ם אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: so that may know all [the] peoples of the earth the hand of Yahweh, that mighty [is] it, so that you may fear Yahweh your God all the days.
pieces: so that all the peoples of the earth may know how mighty the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is, and so that you may fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for all time."

L.24: so that all the peoples of the earth may know the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that it [is] mighty, so that you may fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God all the days."

R.24: He did this so that all the nations of the world will know how powerful {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is, and so that you will always stand in awe of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD: his power at work
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power and action. The phrase recalls the exodus, when the LORD brought Israel out "with a mighty hand" (Exodus 13:9; Deuteronomy 4:34).

decisions.choice: two purposes: that the nations may know, and that Israel may fear
decisions.reason: The wonder is for the whole world to see as well as for Israel. The peoples of Canaan had already heard of the sea (2:9-11) and now hear of the Jordan (5:1). For Israel the purpose is lasting reverence for God.

decisions.choice: so that you may fear: Israel is the one who is to fear
alternatives: so that they [the peoples] may fear the LORD your God
decisions.reason: The verb form in the Hebrew is unusual after "so that". With a small change of its vowels it would read "so that they may fear", carrying on the subject "all the peoples of the earth". The text as written says "you", and that is followed here.

decisions.choice: fear the LORD all the days: revere and obey him always
decisions.reason: To fear the LORD is to stand in awe of him and so to keep his commands (Deuteronomy 6:2, 13, 24). "All the days" means for all time.

decisions.choice: He did this
